append.text: **Ps 103:1b *Confessiónem, et decórem induísti* → *Vestistes-vos de confissão e de esplendor*** — decided with 95:6 as that agent asked: the noun *confissão* in both twins (decision `confessio`; *louvor*, *ação de graças*, *majestade* options). The ambiguity reader heard the sacrament, as at 95:6 — the known cost; the Latinist passed it twice.
**Ps 103:1b → *e de esplendor*** with 92:1a's verb (*Vestistes-vos de*), kept apart from 95:6 *pulchritúdo → beleza*. The Latinist asked *formosura* (v1; refused under this row).

**Ps 103:1 *magnificátus es veheménter* → *fostes muito engrandecido*** (v2: the Latinist asked the passive, and the ambiguity reader heard the reflexive *engrandecestes-vos* as self-aggrandizement, said of God). 103:24 keeps the 91:6 formula *Como se engrandeceram* (the works). Evidence: for God as subject, the passive.

**Ps 103:15 *et panis cor hóminis confírmet* → *e que o pão fortaleça o coração do homem*** (στηρίζει; a heart as object): v1 *sustente* (after 36:17) was refused by the Latinist as feeding rather than strengthening; *fortalecer* (MS1932, DRB) passed the gate. *firme* the option. Evidence that with a heart as object *fortalecer* serves where *firmar* sounds odd.

**Ps 103:14 *Prodúcens fænum juméntis* → *para o gado*** — here *animália* (103:26) needs *animais*, and the Greek keeps θηρία / κτήνη / ζῷα apart, so the row's option *gado* (decision `animals`). *béstiæ → feras* in 103:11, 20 (as 49:10). Proposal: *gado* where *animália* stands in the same psalm.

**Ps 103:24 *impléta est terra possessióne tua* → *a terra se encheu dos vossos bens*** (κτῆσις; as 77:48). The Latinist asked *possessão* twice — refused, heard as demonic possession in Brazil; *posse* the option.
**Ps 103:6 *super montes stabunt aquæ* → *sobre os montes se deterão as águas*** — waters standing still, this row's verb; the Latinist asked *estarão* twice (held as option; flat at the cadence).
**Ps 103:14b *Ut edúcas panem de terra* → *Para que façais sair o pão da terra*** — the stylist asked *tireis*; refused, *tirar* is *auferre*'s (D41) and stands in 103:29.
**Ps 103:13, 16 (χορτάζω) → *se saciará a terra … As árvores do campo se saciarão*** — the stylist found the analytic passive heavy; the medio-passive taken (D2), one form for both verses.

**Ps 103:25 *illic reptília, quorum non est númerus* → *ali rastejam seres sem número*** (no *ómnia* here, so not the row's phrase). The Latinist asked *há répteis* twice — refused as zoological (option).
**Ps 103:19 *sol cognóvit occásum suum* → *o sol conhece o seu poente*** (third person, gnomic); the Latinist asked *conheceu* twice, refused under this ruling.

**Ps 103:22 *in cubílibus suis collocabúntur* → *nos seus covis se deitarão*** (κοιτασθήσονται, animals lying down); *serão colocados* option. Evidence for splitting the row: of lying down → *deitar-se*.
Ps 103:17 *Heródii domus dux est eórum* → *A casa da garça é o guia deles* (kept as the Latin says it).
Ps 103:14 *fænum juméntis* → *feno* (fodder), beside *herbam → erva* in the same verse.
Ps 103:17 *montes excélsi cervis* → *cervos* (the animal context is plain).
Ps 103:5 *stabílitas → firmeza* (v2, stylist) now shares the word in another psalm; see the new *stabílitas* row.

**Ps 103:34 *Jucúndum sit ei elóquium meum* → *Seja-lhe agradável o que digo*** (a man's word; D26's clause in the present). The Latinist (twice) and the stylist asked *a minha palavra*; refused so that *palavra* stays *verbum / sermo*'s; the stylist's weak mediant fixed by dropping *eu*.

terms: | pellis | pele (*Estendendo o céu como uma pele*) | open | Ps 103:2 (δέρριν); the image kept, not explained as a tent (DRB, MS1932 *pavilhão* option). No reader objected; the ambiguity reader missed the tent. |
| superióra (τὰ ὑπερῷα) | as partes altas (*vós que cobris de águas as suas partes altas*) | open | Ps 103:2, 13 (one phrase twice); *alturas* is *excélsa*'s (D42); DRB's *aposentos altos* option. |
| ascénsus | subida (*Vós que pondes a nuvem por vossa subida*) | open | Ps 103:3; *pôr … por* after the stylist (*como* was heard as a simile); DRB *carro* (the Hebrew) option. |

| stabílitas | firmeza (*Vós que fundastes a terra sobre a sua firmeza*) | open | Ps 103:5 (ἀσφάλεια); v1 *estabilidade*, the stylist asked the plainer word; it meets 96:2 *corréctio → firmeza* in another psalm. |

| amíctus (participle / noun) | envolto / manto (*envolto em luz como numa veste … é o seu manto*) | open | Ps 103:1b, 6; no Portuguese pair of one root sounds natural; *vestiméntum → veste* kept in both so the pairing is heard. |
| ónager | asno selvagem (*os asnos selvagens aguardarão na sua sede*) | open | Ps 103:11; *jumento* is a donkey in Brazil, *onagro* unknown. |

| heródius | garça (*A casa da garça é o guia deles*) | open | Ps 103:17; ἐρωδιός, the heron; L&S 'perhaps the stork'; MS1932 *cegonha* (the Hebrew) option. The ambiguity reader found the line unintelligible, as it is in the Latin. |
| herinácius | ouriço (*a rocha, refúgio para os ouriços*) | open | Ps 103:17 (MS1932); the ambiguity reader heard sea urchins; kept. |
| exhilaráre | animar (*Para que anime o rosto com o óleo*) | open | Ps 103:15 (ἱλαρῦναι), kept apart from *lætificáre → alegrar* one colon earlier; *torne alegre* option. |

| emíttere (springs, the spirit) | enviar (*Vós que enviais as fontes nos vales … Enviareis o vosso espírito*) | open | Ps 103:10, 30 (ἐξαποστέλλω both); one verb so the echo is heard; *fazer brotar* option at 103:10. |

| illúdere (+ dative) | brincar com (*Este dragão, que formastes para brincar com ele*) | open | Ps 103:27; *ele* keeps the sea or the dragon open; *zombar dele* (the mocking sense, cf. *illúsio → escárnio*, D39) option. |

| spatiósus mánibus | de largos braços (*Este mar, grande e de largos braços*) | open | Ps 103:25; the Latinist asked *espaçoso de mãos* twice — refused, not Portuguese; *braços de mar* keeps a limb. |

| béstiæ (θηρία) | feras (*todas as feras do campo … todas as feras da selva*) | open | Ps 103:11, 20, as 49:10 *feræ silvárum*; kept apart from *juménta → gado* and *animália → animais* in the same psalm. |
